text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Gabriel Teixeira, head of the Public Security Police (PSP), met Interior Minister Alberto Costa yesterday afternoon to seek ways to resolve the crisis in policing in Portugal.
- The price of leaded "Super" petrol in Portugal rose by 8.38 percent, well above inflation, in the past year.
- PSP general Gabriel Teixeira was given three days to guarantee discipline in the police force in a meeting with Interior Minister Alberto Costa yesterday.
- Banco Espirito Santo cut its variable rate prime rate by 0.375 percentage points to 10.875 percent.

- The newspaper said it had learned that for more than a year, a company called Sub-Productos Minerales S.A. (Suprosa) has stored without a licence tonnes of pyrite ash near the railway station at Aranjuez in Spain, which threaten to contaminate the nearby River Tagus which runs into Portugal.
